question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about the National Pension System (NPS)?

answer.text: It offers guaranteed returns to subscribers
It is a defined contribution retirement savings scheme regulated by PFRDA
It can only invest in government securities

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes NPS as a defined contribution scheme regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA). It is market-linked, offers no defined benefit, and the subscriber's accumulated corpus is invested across multiple asset classes (equity, corporate debt, government securities and alternative assets). The Trap: NPS is regulated by PFRDA, not SEBI. NPS does not guarantee returns - they depend on market performance of the chosen asset mix. NPS is not restricted to G-Secs alone. Note: Pages 94-95 confirm NPS as PFRDA-regulated defined contribution with no defined benefit. Pages 111-112 support multiple asset classes and no guaranteed returns.
